questions.question: The microbes that lie on the border line of the living and non-living world are called:
questions.solution:

• Living things are those which can make movements of their own and perform certain metabolic processes like nutrition, respiration, digestion, etc. to survive.
 
• Human beings, plants, various animals, and microbes like bacteria, fungi, Protozoa, etc come under the category of living things.
 
• Living beings reproduce their offsprings to maintain their race.

**Explanation:**__

The correct answer is __**viruses**__.

__
 
• **Viruses **are considered at the **borderline of living and non-living** because they show **characteristics of both living and non-living.**

• When they enter **living cells**, they start to **reproduce** as living beings by cell multiplication.
 
• They can cause various diseases in human beings, other animals, and plants.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India contains the directive that the State shall make provision for maternity relief?

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India prohibits the Indian State from conferring any title, except a military or academic distinction?

questions.question: Which of the following modes of reproduction is carried out by specialised cells that proliferate to make large number of cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regeneration**__.

__
 
• **Regeneration** is carried out by **specialized cells** that proliferate to **make a large number of cells**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Later on these cells **differentiate **and form **different cell types and tissues**.
 
• **These steps occur in an ordered sequence called development**.
 
• There are** four methods** of **Asexual Reproduction** **fission, fragmentation, regeneration, and spore formation.**
 
• In regeneration events like the** repair of damaged cells, replacement of affected body parts** that are **broken and whole organisms can be reconstructed from a small fragment.**
 
• **Examples of the organism** in which this **process happens are hydra and planaria.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

 
• Layering: In this method, practiced in plants, a stem attached to the parent plant branches out to form new plants. Specialized cells are not involved in making a large number of cells here.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e8a5c295e26ac1de8e8138215094e0f87d9b5bce01cadb29f175d500f1aa17e.png] 
 
• Fission: This is an asexual mode of reproduction where an organism splits into two or more separate entities. The process does not specifically involve specialised cells proliferating to make many cells.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73408d9ca60318ba6d42848cfe40c255fbff0b8bb4940a4af42a12b67f1bc00a.png] 
 
• Fragmentation: In fragmentation, the parent organism breaks into fragments, each capable of growing into a new organism. Although this might sound similar to regeneration, specialised cells specifically proliferating to form many cells is not the primary scenario, unlike in regeneration.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/267c89d97b8f79c7404eb275dd2d98b7dd2ffa283f0624679e32340c0a15c920.png]

questions.question: The unit of calorific value of a fuel is expressed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kJ/kg**__.

__
 
• We know that **when the fuel is burnt** **heat is produced**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The amount **of **heat that different types of fuels produced** on burning are expressed in terms of **calorific value**. 
 
• Thus **Calorific value **of a fuel is the amount of heat produced when **1 gm of fuel is completely burne**d.
 
• **S.I. unit of calorific value of fuels** is **kilojoule per kilogram (KJ/kg)**.
 
• It is calculated by **keeping the pressure constant** and in **normal temperature conditions**.
 
• It is also called **calorific power**. 
 
• For example, **if burning completely one kilogram of wood produces 17 kilojoules of heat, therefore, the calorific value of wood will be 17 KJ/kg.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• psi: Pounds per square inch (pressure)
 
• micron: Micrometer (length)
 
• mmHg: Millimeters of mercury (pressure)
 
• kJ/kg: Kilojoules per kilogram (specific energy)

questions.question: Which of the following is a protein digesting enzyme that is secreted in the small intestine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Trypsin__**.

__
 
• The **food enters into** the body** through the mouth **where teeth cut into small pieces and** salivary glands make it watery.**
 
• It passes through the **oesophagus **which is also called the **food pipe** then food enters the stomach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The food is **partially digested into the stomach and enters the small intestine**.
 
• The **small intestine** is the place where c**omplete digestion happens**. 
 
• **The small intestine has two glands called the liver and pancreas**.
 
• The **liver secretes bile which breaks the fat present in the food into smaller particles so that enzymes can act upon it.**
 
• The **pancreas secretes **two major enzymes called **chymotrypsin and trypsin**.
 
• **Trypsin is a protein-digesting enzyme** that breaks **proteins into simpler substances.**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India specifies the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions?
questions.solution:

__

questions.question: Which of the following amendments to the Constitution of India is also referred to as the 'mini Constitution'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

__
 
• **The 42nd amendment act introduced in 1976** is considered to be one of the** most important amendments to the Indian Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• It came into existence by **Indian National Congress **which was **headed by Indira Gandhi**.
 
• There were **many amendments done in this act during **this time into the constitution so it is also called the **Mini constitution.**
 
• it made changes to the** Preamble, to the seventh schedule of the constitution** and **53 articles were changed in the constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:

 
 
• Provided that the laws made for the implementation of Directive Principles cannot be declared invalid by the courts on the ground of violation of some Fundamental Rights. Hence option 2) is Correct.
 
 
 
• History of cases:
 
 
• Champakam Dorairajan case (1951):
 
 
• Supreme Court ruled that in case of any conflict between the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles, the former would prevail. It declared that the Directive Principles have to conform to and run as subsidiary to the Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• Golaknath case (1967):
 
 
• Court held that the Fundamental Rights cannot be amended for the implementation of the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• Kesavananda Bharati case (1973):
 
 
• Overruled the Judgement of Golaknath Case.
 
 
 
• 42nd Amendment Act (1973):
 
 
• Accorded the **position of legal primacy and supremacy to the Directive Principles over the Fundamental Rights** conferred by Articles **14, 19, and 31.**
 
 
 
• Minerva Mills case (1980):
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** also held that **‘the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles.**
 
• They together constitute the **core of the commitment to social revolution. **
 
• **They are like two wheels of a chariot, one no less than the other.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **It added the words ‘ SOCIALIST’, ‘ SECULAR’ and ‘INTEGRITY’ in the Preamble**.
 
• **Fundamental Duties were also added**.
 
• **Directive Principles **were given **weightage over Fundamental Rights** and any **law made will be out of the scope of judicial review by the court.**
 
• **It made the power of Parliament foremost.**
